title: Ollama and Qwen3.8:27b, can it actually help develop a game from scratch?
author: Mustyyyy
selftext:
I love videogames been all my life and i had this videogame idea for so long but i don't have the time or the ability to start learn to code and develop a game all for my self. *(I did use a lot of RPG Maker in the past and spent years on Roblox Studio in 2016-2018, but still, no expert here, but i do have some basic knowledge on how stuff works under the hood)*

Yesterday i came across this sub and decided to download Ollama and run Qwen3.8:27b locally on my pretty high end desktop.

I downloaded Unity which i know nothing about and laying out the framework, the base of the idea of the game i have, could this actually work? does anyone with little to none game dev experience pulled off some good projects?

comments.author: Trahili
comments.body: Use llama.cpp, Ollama sucks. You're probably not going to be able to use it to code a game unless you know how to code. But you can use Opus 5.5 as an orchestrator giving tasks to it on the $20 a month plan and you should be doing pretty well.

comments.author: shaymagen
comments.body: Honestly I'd skip Unity for a first go and have it build a tiny browser game in a single HTML file, since a local 27B model handles a few hundred lines of JS way better than a whole Unity project, and you can paste errors straight back in. Get one core loop playable first (move, one enemy, a lose condition), then add features one prompt at a time. I run a site of AI-made browser games and wrote up the basic steps here if it helps: https://vibe1up.com/answers/how-to-make-a-game-with-ai/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=comment&utm_campaign=aigamedev
